title: Cech local-lift representative computes the connecting boundary
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let 0 \to A \to B \to C \to 0 be a short exact sequence of sheaves of O_X-modules, let U = {U_i} be an open covering of X, let s in H^0(X,C), and choose lifts t_i in B(U_i) of s|_{U_i}. Then the differences t_{i_1}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}} - t_{i_0}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}} are sections of A and form a Cech 1-cocycle; under the canonical homomorphism c_A from the first Cech cohomology group of U with values in A to H^1(X,A), its class maps to the connecting class partial(s) in the long exact cohomology sequence.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 0B8S (cohomology-lemma-cech-h1), local-lift description of the boundary; compatibility of the Cech-to-cohomology map with the connecting homomorphism

proof.text: Embed B (rather than only A) into an injective I using lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives and the proved Mathlib Injective.under/Injective.ι construction. Put a = f composed with this embedding phi, and T = ShortComplex.mk a (cokernel.π a) (cokernel.condition a). Both f and phi are monic, so a is monic; exact_of_g_is_cokernel applied to cokernelIsCokernel and the epimorphism cokernel.π make T short exact. Exact.desc for the original sequence constructs psi:C to coker(a), satisfying g composed with psi = phi composed with T.g. This gives the short-complex morphism (id_A, phi, psi). All selected injective data come from the proved enough-injectives theorem.

The canonical derived-triangle boundary is natural for this morphism. In the private proved helper singleTrianglePlus_comm₃, apply the faithful inclusion of D⁺ into D and its shift comparison to the third square of Mathlib ShortExact.singleTriangle.map. The private rightDerived_boundary_naturality helper applies the right derived functor to the resulting triangle morphism and invokes lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder, then transports along the natural single-object/right-derived comparison isomorphisms. Specializing this proved calculation to global sections gives boundary_naturality for the exact moduleCohomologyBoundary defined in the statement. Naturality of toRightDerivedZero converts the input section psi(s); the map on A is the identity, so partial_T(psi(s)) = partial_S(s). No arbitrary universal delta-functor boundary is substituted for the recorded triangle boundary.

Set q = psi(s) and x_i = phi(t_i). The equation g composed with psi = phi composed with T.g, the given lift equations, and restriction naturality show that x_i lifts q. Apply lem-sc-boundary-cech-injective-middle to T, q and x_i with the unchanged comparison c and hc; T.X₁ is definitionally A. This supplies a cycle z and its boundary comparison. To recover the original component equation, apply phi on the overlap: T.f is f composed with phi, phi preserves subtraction, and restriction naturality identifies the two right-hand differences. Evaluation of the monomorphism phi is injective on sections, so cancel it. Compose the injective-middle boundary equality with the naturality equality of the preceding step to finish.

split_report.review: The returned E5/C4 gap is repaired: no naturality claim is used to identify a connecting map; Step 1 explicitly invokes naturality of derived connecting morphisms, and Step 3 invokes the dedicated injective-middle statement. The Cech complex is not treated as a resolution of B. Step 1 uses exactly the enough-injectives and universal-delta statements quoted above; Step 2 is the sectionwise elementary comparison; Step 3 uses exactly the injective-middle statement and the same naturality statement. The actual cohomology.tex source was read at Lemma 01EQ (comparison construction), Lemma 01EP (injective Cech acyclicity), and Lemma 0B8S (local-lift formula). The sign is positive because 0B8S writes alpha_{i_0 i_1}=f_{i_0}-f_{i_1}, while the Cech differential is d^0(t)_{i_0 i_1}=t_{i_1}-t_{i_0}; the comparison map conventions identify the former with the boundary as written.
